stories.title: The NTS Interview
stories.description: Ajay recounts his interview for the National Talent Search exam in 10th grade. Instead of asking rote questions, the interviewers asked about his hobbies. When he said 'hacking electronic circuitry', they had a genuine conversation about it, which Ajay felt was the right way to assess a student.

stories.title: Dipan Ghosh's Mechanics
stories.description: Ajay mentions a legendary mechanics teacher at IIT Bombay, Dipan Ghosh. The institute recorded his lectures and distributed them, illustrating that technology can solve the shortage of great teachers.

stories.title: The Chess Puzzle Rating
stories.description: Amit tells a story of Ajay watching him solve chess puzzles on Chess.com. Amit's rating hit 2900, and Ajay, in awe, asked if he was that good in real life. Amit had to explain that puzzle ratings are inflated and his real rating is much lower.

stories.title: Whipped Cream
stories.description: Ajay mentions that during his time at IIT, the students were referred to as the 'whipped cream' (a play on creme de la creme) of the country.

core_ideas.description: Ajay argues that high marks in exams like JEE do not equal merit. They measure conscientiousness and rote learning, not flexible general intelligence or creativity. The system selects for the ability to be regimented.

The root cause of the crisis is the artificial scarcity of higher education seats caused by government restrictions (licensing, non-profit mandate). We need to deregulate so there are enough seats for everyone.

Ajay proposes immediate fixes: 1) Computerized testing (on-demand, multiple attempts), 2) Item Response Theory (better statistical estimation of ability), and 3) Private testing agencies (better logistics).

Ajay and Nitin Pai propose a radical solution: A qualifying exam to select the top 100,000 students (based on conceptual understanding), followed by a random lottery to pick the 20,000 for IITs. This would reduce stress and increase diversity.
Universities should have the autonomy to decide their own admissions criteria (interviews, essays, etc.) rather than being forced to use a single centralized exam.

jokes_and_cultural_references.context: Amit compares banning coaching classes to banning paracetamol for a fever—it attacks the symptom, not the root cause.
Ajay compares students who rote-learn question patterns to the 'fastest gun in the West', able to shoot (solve) quickly without thinking.
